title: Hunt for the Wilderpeople
tagline: Bush life. Bush tucker for the trip.
about: A city foster kid and his grumpy uncle become the target of a national manhunt in the New Zealand bush.
cue: Serve the roast when Bella brings home the pig.
faces: Uncle Hec, I'm a real gangster, but I'll still have seconds. Writing a haiku about this stew.

    StartersRicky's camp oven damperHollow-crusted bush bread served warm with butter and golden syrupHow to make it60g butter, cold, for the dough40g butter, to serve450g self-raising flour1 tsp salt300ml milk125ml golden syrupRub the cold butter for the dough into the flour and salt.Stir in the milk to a soft dough and shape into a round. Cut a cross on top.Bake at 200°C until it sounds hollow.Serve warm, torn, with the butter to serve and golden syrup.Wild pork sausage rollsPork, green apple and sage rolled in flaky puff pastryHow to make it500g pork sausage mince1 green apple, grated1 onion, finely diced1 tbsp sage, chopped2 sheets of puff pastry1 egg, beatenMix the sausage mince with the apple, onion and sage.Roll into logs along the pastry sheets and roll up, then cut each into 6.Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C until golden.Rest briefly before serving.Curried egg and watercress sandwichesLunch at the hut in the rangesHow to make itAs written, serves 4Soft white bread filled with chopped egg in a mild curry mayo with chives, packed with peppery watercress, cut into triangles and wrapped for the tramp.Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.Chop roughly and mash with 100g mayo, 1 tsp mild curry powder, 2 tbsp chopped chives, salt and pepper.Butter 12 slices of soft white bread.Spread the egg over 6 slices, top with a good handful of watercress and close the sandwiches.Cut into triangles and wrap in baking paper.MainsBella's roast porkSlow-roasted pork shoulder with crackling, green apples and kūmaraHow to make it1.5kg pork shoulder2 tsp salt2 green apples, quartered2 onions, quartered800g kumara, in chunks1 tbsp plain flour250ml water or stockScore the pork and rub with salt, then leave uncovered in the fridge, which is the resting time.Roast at 230°C.Reduce to 170°C and roast on a bed of apple and onion, adding the kumara for the last hour.Make gravy with the flour, water and pan juices.Hāngī-style lamb and kūmaraA feed for the whole search partyHow to make itAs written, serves 4Lamb shoulder, kūmara, pumpkin and cabbage wrapped tight and slow roasted with garlic and rosemary until the meat falls apart, with the rich pan juices spooned over.Heat the oven to 160°C.Rub a 2kg bone-in lamb shoulder with salt, pepper, 4 crushed garlic cloves and rosemary.Line a deep roasting tin with foil and cabbage leaves.Add the lamb, 800g kūmara and 600g pumpkin in big chunks and 250ml water.Cover with more cabbage leaves and seal tightly with foil.Roast 4 hours.Pull the lamb into chunks and spoon the juices over everything.SweetsBella's birthday cakeChocolate cake with cocoa buttercream icing and candlesHow to make it200g butter, softened, for the cake200g caster sugar3 eggs250g self-raising flour50g cocoa powder, for the cake200ml milk250g icing sugar25g cocoa powder, for the icing50g butter, softened, for the icing1 pack birthday candlesBeat the cake butter and sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour, the cake cocoa and milk.Bake in a 22cm tin at 175°C.Cool completely.Beat the icing sugar, icing cocoa and icing butter with a splash of milk until smooth and ice the cake.Add candles and sing badly.DrinksRicky Baker haiku hot cocoaHot milk whisked with cocoa and sugar until steamingHow to make it4 tbsp cocoa powder4 tbsp caster sugar1 L milkWhisk the
